lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Hello again! Tilly here. Today's tale takes us far beyond the Earth's <color=red>atmosphere</color>.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Read it closely, then answer four questions. Answer them all <color=red>accurately</color> and four new books will land on the library shelves.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Dr Imani Osei had spent six months alone aboard a research station <color=red>orbiting</color> Jupiter, measuring the vast storms that swirl across its surface.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Her mission was nearly over when the station's main telescope began sending back <color=red>distorted</color> images. Rather than wait weeks for engineers on Earth to advise her, she decided to investigate herself.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: The fault turned out to be a speck of frozen dust on the lens. Imani melted it away with a gentle stream of warm air and <color=red>recalibrated</color> the instrument by hand.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: That night, the telescope captured the clearest image of Jupiter's Great Red Spot ever recorded. Imani labelled it simply: "Patience, then <color=red>ingenuity</color>."

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 1: What was Imani studying from the research station?
lines.hint: Not quite. Reread the first part of the story.
lines.correctText: Correct. She was measuring the storms on Jupiter.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 2: Why did Imani decide to investigate the fault herself?
choices: Advice from Earth would take weeks
lines.hint: Not quite. Think about what she chose not to wait for.
lines.correctText: Yes. Help from the engineers on Earth would have taken weeks.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 3: What was causing the problem with the telescope?
choices: A speck of frozen dust on the lens
lines.hint: Not quite. Look at what she melted away.
lines.correctText: Exactly. A single speck of frozen dust was to blame.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 4: In the story, what does <color=red>distorted</color> most nearly mean?
lines.hint: Not quite. The images were caused by a fault. Use that as a clue.
lines.correctText: Well reasoned. The images were twisted and unclear.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Four for four. Your reading is nothing short of <color=red>astronomical</color>. Four new books are touching down in the library as we speak.

afterLines.speaker: Tilly
afterLines.text: Thank you for voyaging with me. The library's collection is growing at a truly <color=red>impressive</color> rate.
